subject: Quarterly review prep — runway sanity check & account-by-account playbook
messages:
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-11T08:12:00Z
Subject: Quarterly review prep — runway sanity check & account-by-account playbook

Team —

We're a little over a week from the Quarterly Review readout. I need a compact, account-by-account pack for ACME (priority) and two other top deals for the leadership deck. The deliverables I want by EOD Tuesday (2028-05-16):

- a one-slide: executive snapshot per account with ARR, current commit, nearest risk (top 3), and recommended mitigation
- consolidated forecast worksheet (single tab) with staged probabilities and last-call adjustments (include your confidence score 0.0-1.0)
- a short playbook (3 bullets) for the next 30 days per account — who owns what, immediate asks, and expected tickets to close

Karthik: can you own the ACME rollup? Use the attached template and include the finalized MSA effective date.
Tessa: please coordinate CS touches and include the latest adoption metrics for the three accounts.
Naomi: please sanity-check numbers against the billing ledger and flag any ARR recognition timing issues.
Priya: I'll loop you on procurement for ACME; if they surface additional terms we should anticipate a procurement timeline.

Keep slides tight. My goal is to have a 10-slide appendix to the QBR that leadership can flip to for detail. If there's a red account, mark it with an explicit action owner and a two-week escalation path.

—Markus
Markus Klein | Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: forecast_notes_0508.md (see attached notes)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-11T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quarterly review prep — runway sanity check & account-by-account playbook

On 2028-05-11, Markus Klein wrote:
> Karthik: can you own the ACME rollup? Use the attached template and include the finalized MSA effective date.

Yep — taking point. Quick status:
- Latest ACME numbers attached (acme_account_rollup_v2.xlsx). I reconciled the field forecast against the contract team and updated the MSA effective date to 2028-05-01.
- Risk: procurement is asking for a shorter data residency clause which may trigger legal review. I note this under risks and gave it a 0.55 confidence impact on close timing (see worksheet).
- Playbook: three immediate asks are (1) finalize SSO testing window with CS, (2) commit to pilot scope and success metrics, (3) procurement target sign-off date.

I'll circulate a slide draft by Monday EOD (2028-05-14) so we have time to iterate. If ACME procurement surfaces a last-minute term, I'll escalate to you and Priya.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_account_rollup_v2.xlsx

From: sophie.harrell@acme-corp.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-05-12T09:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Quarterly review prep — runway sanity check & account-by-account playbook

Hi Karthik / Markus —

Thanks for the note and the updated MSA date. From procurement's side we have two asks:
1) small change to Section 4.2 (data residency) — prefer EU-only for the pilot, expanding later
2) clarification on liability cap for PII processing during pilot

We can sign the pilot MSA by 2028-05-25 if those clarifications are handled quickly. I'm copying Brian from Atlas who will help with the SSO timeline.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Harrell | Director, AI Platforms
ACME Corp

Attachment: none

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-12T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Quarterly review prep — runway sanity check & account-by-account playbook

Markus / team —

I pulled adoption metrics and included the three-slide CS summary in the Drive link (see related_links). Highlights:
- ACME usage: pilot success metric (LLM inference ops) currently at 42% of target throughput due to SSO delay — flagged as a medium risk
- Two other accounts (Eastside Health, Nebula Analytics) have clean adoption curves; Eastside asked for a model quantization proofpoint before expanding — added to playbook
- I propose we call out ACME as a "watch" in the deck and lay out the two-week remediation steps for SSO + legal gating

I'll update the slide for ACME with the adoption chart and send v1 to Karthik Monday morning.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan | Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-13T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quarterly review prep — runway sanity check & account-by-account playbook

Quick procurement update on ACME: I spoke to Sophie and procurement@acme-corp.com this morning. Their legal team is willing to accept our standard liability language if we include a scoped pilot exception for data residency that restricts EU data to our EU-hosted nodes for the first 90 days.

Action items for us:
- Karthik: add the pilot exception language to the MAP and confirm with ACME today
- Naomi: confirm billing alignment for the 90-day pilot (especially around usage-based credits)
- Markus: if legal asks to see a precedent, I can surface the SmallPilot addendum we used with Nebula (link in related_links).

I'll collate the procurement timeline into the MAP and upload the signed stub if they approve. Looks doable to keep ACME on the May sign path.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan | Head of Strategic Procurement
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf
